recipes.name: Crispy Flautas
ingredients_raw: 1 pound skinless, boneless chicken breast, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 (10 ounce) package corn tortillas (such as Ortega®)

steps.text: Heat 1 teaspoon vegetable oil in a skillet over medium heat. Stir in the bell pepper and onion; cook and stir until the onion has softened and turned translucent, about 5 minutes. Increase heat to medium-high and stir in the chicken breast. Cook and stir until the chicken breast is no longer pink in the center, about 10 minutes. Shred the chicken using two forks. Stir in the taco seasoning and water. Simmer until the liquid has evaporated, stirring occasionally, about 10 minutes. Stir in the Cheddar cheese, then remove from heat, and set aside.

Lightly brush each corn tortilla will a layer of salsa. Spread about 2 tablespoons of the chicken mixture in a line along the bottom edge of the tortilla. Tightly roll the tortilla into a cylinder, and secure the ends with one or two toothpicks. Repeat with remaining tortillas.
Heat 2 cups vegetable oil in a large skillet to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).

Fry the flautas in the preheated oil, no more than 4 at a time, until golden and crisp, about 4 minutes. Drain the flautas on a paper towel-lined plate. Discard toothpicks and top finished flautas with remaining salsa.

raw_recipe.headline: Crispy Flautas
raw_recipe.description: Corn tortillas are filled with shredded seasoned chicken, cheese, and your favorite salsa, then fried to a golden crisp.

review.reviewBody: Traditionally I do believe Flautas are made with flour tortillas and Taquitos with corn tortillas. At least in Southern California these would be considered taquitos. I used cooked left over chicken. Minced very small. Minced the onion and bell pepper small. Cooked the onion, bell pepper - added the chicken and taco seasoning and cooked a bit. Added about 1/4 cup water and cooked it down - add a little more water if it seems to be drying out. Take off the heat and stir in the cheese. For the tortillas - I heated the oil and dipped each tortilla briefly in the hot oil - remove quickly so they don't start to brown. Place a spoonful of chicken on to each tortilla roll up and place seam side down on paper towels. Do NOT overfill. Once all the tortillas are rolled start frying by placing into the oil seam side DOWN - 3 or 4 at a time - this seals the tortilla. Once brown and crispy, flip and fry the other side. Drain on paper towels and serve with salsa on the side.

Instead of using corn tortillas, I used flour tortillas. I did not fry them. I experimented with my air fryer and found that it worked perfectly for the Falutas! That's the way for me to go from now on!

I made these for the first time last night, 3/6/2015. This is a fantastic recipe. The only thing I did differently was fry corn tortillas on each side for a couple of seconds before adding my chicken mixture. I was so surprised how fresh they tasted compared to the ones you get in a restaurant. Also, I made my own taco mixture with 1 tbs of chili powder, 1/2 tbs of onion powder and 1/2 tbs of cumin. Nothing can compare to home cooked, we love these and will use them as an appetizer next time we have a dinner party. 
I made mexican rice as a side and guacamole- 3 avocados, 3-4 chopped onions, 1 Serrano, 1/2 squeezed lime or lemon, and about 1 tbs of my homemade hot sauce, and a chopped tomato. Season with salt, pepper, cumin to taste. If the serrano has too much heat, use a regular jalepeno. So good.
Have now made this with pork and beef too. Can't beat this recipe. Used my air fryer instead of oil frying, Great.

My teenaged boys both *loved* these. I followed the suggestion of another user to lightly fry the corn tortillas, then fill, roll and fry again. I wasn't wild about the taste or consistency of the filling. I think because it was all minced, it was mushy and didn't have a lot of flavor. Next time, I think I'm going to use shredded roast beef. The only other thing I added was a sprinkle of kosher salt once the taquitos came out of the oil the second time. The salt sticks well if they're still hot! Like a couple of other commenters, I don't buy the taco seasoning at the store but make my own. So much better! Thank you for the recipe Baking Nana!

Yes. Baking Nana is correct. Flautas Are flour tortillas not corn. So with that said, I too had leftover chicken. I added a couple teaspoon of dried onion, chicken tacos seasoning and some chipotle powder. I didn't bother with toothpicks, just held them together with tongs till they could hold their own shape. Drained and served with guacamole n sour cream. I made Fideo to go with it. Delish! Thanks KCB

I made these using green Enchillada sauce, and some cumin for seasoning, instead of the Taco seasoning and water and they were delicious.I also used flour tortillas instead of corn tortillas I will definately make this again. They were even better the next day after sitting for a while in the fridge- I just reheated them in the oven to keep them crispy ( don't reheat in the microwave or they will go soggy). Served with lots of guacamole and they were to die for

These were great, didn't use toothpicks and if you find the tortillas are tearing it may be that you are not using them at room temperature.

I used the hatch chili shredded chicken my store carries in the deli to save some time and it came out fabulously. I serve with guacamole, salsa and sour cream, and a salad with a cilantro, lime dressing and they disappear quickly.

Loved these. I used my usual mix for the chicken seasoning and added sweet onion and garlic. Also, used a bare minimum of oil to fry, maybe 1/4 c. and they were nice and crunchy! Thanks for the recipe, may try beef/cheese mix with flour tortillas next time.

Used ground turkey instead of chicken, red pepper instead of green, flour tortillas instead of corn. super delicious.
Update: Tried with ground beef. Boyfriend liked it even better.

We had to turn the temperature down on the fryer to 350 because otherwise the stuff started burning. Also had difficulty the first few times trying to wrap it because the corn tortillas kept tearing (probably user error more than anything :-P). But overall, definitely liked!!!
This was so good! I keft the recioe the same but I used queso Blanco and Mexican crema to dip them in, since that's what my Mexican friend had showed me.

Let me start by saying my grandsons are picky eaters. Even they enjoyed this! We were so hungry from smelling it cooking, I didn't even take a picture. Definitely a hit. I'm sending the recipe to my daughter to cook for my other grandkids. Easy to make and very tasty!

The taste wasn't to bad, but hubby said it was to much work. The corn tortillas were hard to work with also. We thought about trying with flour tortillas, but we have much better recipes if we want to fry tortillas.
The kids loved them! We topped ours with lettuce, tomatoes, guacamole and salsa. Thanks for the recipe!
Delicious!
Our family loved these and have even shared with other family and friends.
These are just as good as the ones at Taco Cabana! Seriously. Super simple to make.
This came out sooo good..i didn't have corn tortillas so I used flour tortillas..
Tortillas broke after a few min. Never made it to the fryer.
